Let me work through this systematically.

**Three-letter Roman numeral palindromes** have the form ABA (first and last letters identical). Since Roman numerals use {I, V, X, L, C, D, M}, and V, L, D cannot repeat, A must be one of **I, X, C, M**.

Checking all ABA combinations for validity:

| Numeral | Value | Valid? |
|---------|-------|--------|
| III | 3 | ✓ |
| IVI | 7 | ✗ (written VII) |
| IXI | — | ✗ (invalid) |
| XIX | 19 | ✓ (X + IX) |
| XVX | 25 | ✗ (written XXV) |
| XXX | 30 | ✓ |
| XLX | 50 | ✗ (written L) |
| XCX | 100 | ✗ (written C) |
| CIC | 201 | ✗ (written CCI) |
| CXC | 190 | ✓ (C + XC) |
| CCC | 300 | ✓ |
| CDC | 500 | ✗ (written D) |
| CMC | 1000 | ✗ (written M) |
| MIM | 2001 | ✗ (written MMI) |
| MCM | 1900 | ✓ (M + CM) |
| MDM | 2500 | ✗ (written MMD) |
| MMM | 3000 | ✓ |

**Valid palindromic Roman numerals:** III, XIX, XXX, CXC, CCC, MCM, MMM

**Sum:** 3 + 19 + 30 + 190 + 300 + 1900 + 3000 = **5442**

arguments.content:
The three-letter Roman numerals that read the same forwards and backwards are:

  III  =    3
  XIX  =   19
  XXX  =   30
